title: Assignment maps for arbitrary reduced quantum dynamics
abstract: Given an open quantum system $S$ with environment $E$, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) maps from $S$ to $E$ and assignment maps initializing the composite system $SE$ in a possibly correlated state prior to unitary evolution. We show that every possible joint state $ρ_{SE}$ can be realized by such assignment maps, which are inherently Hermiticity-preserving and trace-preserving (HPTP). While these maps sacrifice global positivity, we derive a simple necessary and sufficient condition for any local state of $S$ to belong to their domain of validity. Furthermore, we prove that the geometry of this domain is governed by the joint state assigned to the maximally mixed input, ensuring that a non-zero volume of admissible local states can readily coexist with initial system-environment entanglement. Finally, we provide an operational protocol for witnessing such limits of validity.
summary: This paper develops a general theory connecting standard reduced quantum dynamics (CPTP maps) to 'assignment maps' that account for initial correlations between the system and environment. It proves a one-to-one mapping between these two descriptions and rigorously characterizes the domain of local states that are physically accessible given initial entanglement. This resolves limitations in modeling open quantum systems by providing a precise geometric constraint on valid local preparations.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a systematic mathematical framework for describing reduced quantum dynamics in open systems when initial system-environment correlations are present.
main_result: A one-to-one correspondence is established between physical CPTP maps and kinematical assignment maps, which are required to be Hermiticity-preserving and trace-preserving (HPTP).
method: The authors utilize the Choi matrix formalism and the concept of an 'assignment map' ($A$) acting as a reverse shift from the local system description to the global system-environment state.
model_or_system: The system involves an open quantum system $S$ interacting with an environment $E$. The dynamics are generally described by CPTP maps, but the analysis extends to initial correlations captured by a joint state $ho_{SE}$.
key_observables: The domain of validity ($	ext{dov}(A_E)$) of the assignment map, which dictates physically accessible local preparations.
important_parameters: The joint reference state $R_E$ assigned to the maximally mixed input, which governs the geometry of the domain of validity.
main_assumptions: The approach requires treating the assignment map $A$ as kinematical rather than strictly dynamical, and the domain is determined by the positivity of the anticommutator involving the reference state.
paper_structure: The paper builds the correspondence between CPTP maps and assignment maps, derives the necessary and sufficient condition for local state validity based on the reference state, and concludes with an operational protocol for testing these limits.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical tool to analyze open quantum systems beyond the standard assumption of product initial states, which is crucial for understanding realistic quantum dynamics.
